correctness.rationale: The exact corner decomposition is conditioned on every edge having at least two samples, whose complement has exponentially small probability. Disjoint boundary-strip survival functions yield joint independent exponential gaps, the continuous mapping theorem proves the joint limit, and uniform exponential tails plus negligible exceptional event yield all mixed fixed moments. A double integral proves the exponentially accurate mean. The gamma-product large-deviation sandwich rigorously recovers the largest coefficient from the area tail, and Laplace-factor induction identifies the remaining angle sines. The checker reconstructs convex hulls but is only corroborative.

originality.rationale: A comparison of the primary 2019/2023 mean-volume-deficit theorem with the 2025 Hausdorff-distance result and relevant interior-sampling literature reveals no full joint law or inverse angle signature. Targeted semantic searches return only distinct metrics/models. Some ingredients are classical and priority is provisional: the claimed contribution is the combined distributional, quantitative and inverse classification, not the elementary fact that nearest boundary gaps are asymptotically exponential.

value.rationale: Unlike previous mean missed-volume and Hausdorff-maximum results, the theorem gives a complete joint distribution for two intrinsic metrics of the same random approximants. Its area marginal is an inverse geometric statistic: it determines every angle sine and exactly the triangle similarity class. This provides a structural classification and sharp angular extremum rather than a routine reformulation of an expected-value computation.
